title: Annotatio II §.V: Bayer concession — first oral reception of the proper body, yet for the faithful only
pass_a_gloss: Although meanwhile this is to be conceded to Bayer as alleged: that Paschasius Radbertus was the first who taught that the properly so-called Body of Christ is received in the Sacred Supper with the mouth of the body — and indeed without laceration to be done by the teeth (On the body and blood of Christ ch. 4) — yet with oral reception also restricted to the faithful alone (same book ch. 6), having professed in express words (ch. 10) that that food (namely Christ’s flesh) is offered only to Christ’s friends and brothers alone.
pass_b_english: Concede to Bayer this much: Paschasius is first to teach oral reception of Christ’s proper body in the Supper without tooth-laceration.
Even then he restricts oral reception to the faithful alone — that food only for Christ’s friends and brothers.
source_text: Quanquam interea illud allegato Bajero concedendum sit Paschasium Rhadebertum, primum fuisse, qui propriè dictum Corpus Christi, in S. Coena, Ore corporis, accipi docuerit, & quidem citra lacerationem, dentibus instituendam, libro de corpore & sanguine Christi cap. 4. restricta tamen etiam Orali acceptione ad solos fideles, lib. eodem cap. 6., cibum istum (nempe carnem Christi) non nisi solis amicis & fratribus Christi porrigi, disertis verbis cap. 10. professus.

lemmas.gloss: with the mouth of the body
